slides.texte_overlay:
Hobbies that quietly
make you a genius
Playing chess. Every game is a lesson in planning, patience and seeing a few moves ahead. Start online or at a local club.
Learning a foreign language. New words, new grammar, new ways of thinking. A second language stretches your brain like nothing else.
Photography. Light, composition, timing. Learning to really see the world trains attention and creativity at the same time.
Gardening. Planning, patience and learning from mistakes. Growing your own food teaches biology, chemistry and calm. Start with herbs.
Daily micro-learning. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it connects all my other hobbies together.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It connects all my other hobbies together.

slides.texte_overlay: Solving puzzles. Crosswords, Rubik's cubes, logic games. Ten minutes a day keeps your mind quick and flexible. Keep one in your bag.
Writing a journal. Putting thoughts into words makes you think more clearly and understand yourself better. Five minutes before bed is enough.
